w: At 5.15 pm a unique Guru Bhakti Din program by kishores commenced in the mandir hall. It was a unique celebration in honor of Swamishri on the occasion of Guru Purnima. The central theme was Swamishri's divine life and work. Incidents of Swamishri's devotion to his guru Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj were narrated by two kishore comperes and Swamishri himself. Video interviews and live addresses by senior sadhus and devotees further enlightened the audience about Swamishri's humility, atmanishtha, compassion, purity and love for kishores. The three-hour program was punctuated with impressive slide and video presentations. The celebration climaxed with Swamishri's blessings: "The program presentation here today has become possible because of the blessings of Yogiji Maharaj. It is through his benedictions that balaks, kishores and youths have been touched by Satsang. The great holy sadhus have always desired to make all souls happy. They have explained that your happiness lies within. True happiness is the happiness of God..." More than 8,500 devotees had attended the memorable, spiritually elevating program.
Bal - Balika Din During Swamishri’s morning puja balaks sang kirtans and played musical instruments.

During the evening Bal Din assembly, balaks presented a drama that symbolised the search for true happiness. They explained that true happiness does not lie in worldly pleasures, but in spirituality. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly stating, “All worldly pleasures are accompanied by misery. However, one who takes the refuge of God and His holy Sadhu, and follows the tenets laid down by scriptures, will ultimately attain happiness.”

To return the love and care Swamishri gives to children, they expressed their affection for him on Bal-Balika Din. Dozens of balaks displayed their talent and conveyed messages through programs that would benefit all children

Balaks showed their love for Swamishri from the early morning as he made his way for morning darshan, by forming a human train and escorting him to the mandir murtis. Thereafter, Swamishri proceeded to his morning puja during which young balaks sang kirtans and played musical instruments.

During the evening assembly, balaks presented a drama that symbolized the search for true happiness. They explained that true happiness does not lie in mere worldly pleasures, but in spirituality, and they also invited all balaks to be a part of BAPS children's activities.

Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly stating that all worldly pleasure is accompanied by misery. However, one who takes the refuge of God and His Saint, and follows the tenets laid down by scriptures, will ultimately attain happiness.

A youth, Atul Ajmera, said to Swamishri, “Today I climbed all the way up to the first shikhar of the Akshardham monument. It was cool when I was at the top, but when I climbed down again, I felt hot.”

Hearing this Swamishri said, “Now understand. Whenever you go up it is always cool. Down here on Earth it is always hot and disturbing. We should have one aim – to go to Akshardham. When we go there it is cool forever.”

ds.t: Seven years instead of six months
w: Balkrishna Shriya, the father in law of Ravi Ruia, owner of the Essar Group, and owner of the LML scooter company, came for darshan. When his wife was extremely ill, he had taken her to America for treatment. At that time our devoted youth C. J. Patel, on Swamishri's instruction, had served them a great deal. At that time Swamishri too had blessed Balkrishnabhai, "Your wife's life will be extended." The doctors had given her only 6 months, but with Swamishri's blessings she lived for seven years.

This divine grace of Pramukh Swami Maharaj stays in his heart, and that is why, whenever the sadhus go to his city, he has always given them his full cooperation in every way. Today, having come for Swamishri's darshan, he asked for blessings that his devotion would keep growing. Swamishri was pleased.
Chandrakantbhai Pujara, a devoted devotee from London, came for darshan. He said, "After going to Akshardham, I want to come back here again, so that I can do more and more seva."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Come if it is Maharaj's command."
Chandrakantbhai said, "Please write a note for it!"
Swamishri said in Hindi, "That has to be an order. A note cannot be written like that."

Swamishri tied a nadachhadi (sacred thread) on his wrist. In the same way, Swamishri also tied a nadachhadi on his nephew Kumarbhai. While tying the nadachhadi, Swamishri said, "The bondage of the world is released, and you have come into the bond of God."

ds.t: Freed from the bonds of the world
w: Chandrakantbhai Pujara, a devoted devotee from London, came for darshan. He said, "After going to Akshardham, I want to come back here again, so that I can do more and more seva."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Come if it is Maharaj's command."

Swamishri tied a nadachhadi (sacred thread) on him. In the same way Swamishri also tied a nadachhadi on his nephew Kumarbhai. While tying the nadachhadi, Swamishri said, "The bondage of the world is gone, and you have come into the bond of Bhagwan."
Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was moving towards the place of puja, the sadhus introduced a devotee: "This is Sulabh Patel."
Seeing him, Swamishri asked, "Are you from Nadiad?"
"No, Swami! From Houston."
"Where did you live before?" Swamishri probed deeper.
Sulabhbhai said, "Yes, Swami! From 1994 to 1998 I lived in the organisation's hostel in Nadiad."
Everyone was astonished.

This was from 20 years ago. When would Swamishri have met Sulabhbhai? How many times would he have met him? And besides, how many students must have passed through the Nadiad hostel between '94 and '98!? Who would remember who was met where and who lived where? At first even Sulabhbhai himself had forgotten, but Swamishri remembered. Truly, there is no match for Swamishri's power of memory.
